sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Focuses on TIMSS 2015 Grade 8 (Year 9 / Form 3) students in Malta. The main study was administered in April 2015 and included all students in the cohort attending state and non-state schools; 82 students were excluded or withdrawn for not satisfying selection criteria and 164 were absent on the assessment day, leaving 3,817 assessed students. The report also notes that the international benchmarks analysis excludes the seven benchmarking entities (Florida, Quebec, Ontario, Dubai, Buenos Aires, Abu Dhabi) from cross-country comparisons.

data.outcome_summary: This document is a TIMSS 2015 Malta national report describing students’ achievement and contextual factors rather than training or evaluating machine-learning models. It uses TIMSS 2015 Grade 8 (Year 9 / Form 3) mathematics and science assessments administered in April 2015 to 3,817 Maltese students, with achievement scaled on the TIMSS scale (mean 500, SD 100) and interpreted via international benchmarks at 400/475/550/625. The report summarizes mean scores, percentile distributions, and benchmark attainment, and compares Malta to the international average and to other participating countries (excluding benchmarking entities). It also reports relationships between achievement and questionnaire-derived scales (e.g., home resources, language of the test at home, school resources, teacher job satisfaction, safety/order, bullying, and student belonging), but the provided excerpt does not specify PV combining rules or missing-data handling procedures. Policy implications emphasize strengthening mathematics and science attainment, reducing low-benchmark proportions, and improving instructional and resource conditions, while noting that the next cycle (TIMSS 2019) would be computer-based.
